newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota faces water rationing as rains lash down.
newsitem.headline: Bogota faces water rationing as rains lash down.

text.p: Bogota's eight million citizens may be faced with emergency water rationing within a week as an indirect result of torrential rains, which have lashed the city since early January, Mayor Antanas Mockus said on Sunday.

Freak conditions have brought as much as six times the average rainfall to Bogota during what is normally Colombia's dry season. Earlier this month, a mudslide blocked a tunnel that brings water from the city's main reservoir.

An Italian-Venezuelan company began excavating the tunnel on Sunday but Mockus said work would last at least a month. The Bogota Water Company estimates supplies in an emergency reservoir will run out by the first week of March.
Mockus told the NTC-TV news programme that requests for citizens to cut water usage by 20 percent appeared to have fallen on deaf ears.
"We are going to have to bring in a two-phase rationing system to cut water consumption and if that doesn't work then we will just have to introduce a crisis plan," Mockus said.

He did not give details of the proposed rationing system, although he called on Bogota's inhabitants not to wash cars and houses or water lawns. The water utility has said it will progressively reduce the pressure in Bogota's mains.
